title: How Do X-Rays See Inside Your Bones? 🦴
description: How do X-rays reveal broken bones without touching your body? Discover the physics of X-ray imaging and how shadows expose your skeleton in seconds.

scenes.say: How do we snap a clear picture of your bones without a single cut? The secret hides inside a beam of invisible energy!

scenes.caption: X-ray vacuum tube
scenes.say: It all starts inside a vacuum tube. Fast-moving electrons slam into a heavy metal target to generate pure X-ray energy.
As rays pass through you, they cruise right through skin and muscle. But the dense calcium in your bones blocks them completely.
The surviving rays hit a digital sensor behind you, turning dark while your bones leave behind a bright white shadow.
Scientist Wilhelm Röntgen named them X because they were a total mystery when he first discovered them!
